evidence: src/middlewares/bodySchemaValidator.ts: bodySchemaValidator(schema) returns an Express (req, res, next) handler, which is a presentation-layer middleware.
The statement `schema.validate(req.body)` checks the shape of the request body against a schema passed in by the caller. The file defines no domain rules of its own.
It throws { name: "ValidationError", message: error.details } when validation fails, which is transport-level error signalling.
There is no persistence or data access and no business logic. The file is only used by routers (cardsRouter, statementsRouter).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is an Express middleware in the presentation layer. Its only job is to check the incoming request body against a Joi schema that the caller passes in. If the check fails it throws a ValidationError, and otherwise it calls next(). Checking the shape of request input is transport and presentation work. The file has no business rules, because the schema is supplied by the router, and it has no persistence logic. All of its responsibilities fit the presentation layer.
